question.problem: A cat’s position relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by the function $x(t)=3{t}^{2}+t$ meters, where $t$ is the time in hours. Find the average position of the cat between $2$ and $4$ hours.
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the position on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{x}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}\,{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{4-2}\,{\int }_{2}^{4}(3{t}^{2}+t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{({t}^{3}+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2})|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[({4}^{3}+\frac{{4}^{2}}{2})-({2}^{3}+\frac{{2}^{2}}{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[(64+8)-(8+2)] \\  & =31.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average position is $31\,\text{m}.$
